newsitem.title: UK: Thatcher free enterprise chair at Cambridge.
newsitem.headline: Thatcher free enterprise chair at Cambridge.

text.p: Former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher is giving almost 2 million pounds ($3.4 million) to Cambridge University to set up studies in her own particular brand of free enterprise economics.
"It is designed to make Cambridge a world centre, the repository of all the knowledge and conditions in which enterprise flourishes around the world," a Thatcher aide told The Sunday Times.
The professorship, attached to the university's management study school, is being financed by a 1.9 million pound grant from the Margaret Thatcher Foundation.
"A lot of people, Lady Thatcher included, are concerned that the practice of capitalism, particularly in Russia and large parts of China, exemplifies the capitalism of the cowboy," the aide said.
"This chair is designed to teach that capitalism does have a moral and legal basis." ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
